items.prompt: White has three pieces developed and Black none. Black has spent his moves on the queenside. Find the sacrifice that uses White's lead.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is Bxf7+.
Bxf7+ wins material in the engine's best line.
The next best move, Ne5, is at least 1.5 pawns worse.

hints: Which Black pawn is defended only by the king?
Which White piece already eyes f7?
Bxf7+ Kxf7 Ne5+ and the king is exposed.
items.explain: Black's knight and bishops are still at home, so the king has no helpers. Bxf7+ is the engine's first choice and wins material in its best line; the next best move is at least 1.5 pawns worse.

items.prompt: Black has also played ...Nf6. Does the sacrifice Bxf7+ still work? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bxf7+ is at least two pawns worse than the best move.

hints: Which Black piece has joined the defence?
After Bxf7+ Kxf7, can White keep attacking?
The king reaches g8 and White has only given up a piece.
items.explain: With the knight on f6 the Black king has a safe square and White has no follow-up. The engine rates Bxf7+ at least two pawns below the best move. One extra developed defender changes the verdict.

items.prompt: Black's knight is on f6 and his bishop on g4. White to move: does Bxf7+ win material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bxf7+ is at least three pawns worse than the best move.
The engine rates the position as roughly level.

hints: Compare this position with the demonstration: which Black piece has moved?
Who defends f7 and the king now?
The knight on f6 gives the king room and covers key squares.
items.explain: The same sacrifice that worked in the demonstration fails once Black has a knight on f6: Bxf7+ is at least three pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is O-O.
Qe2 is at least 0.8 pawns worse.
Kf1 is at least one pawn worse.

hints: White's king is still in the centre and Black can open the centre with ...dxe4.
Which move puts the king on a safe square and brings a rook into play?
Castle kingside.
items.explain: With the e-pawn on e4, Black can open the centre at once and White's king is still on e1. O-O is the engine's first choice; Qe2 is at least 0.8 pawns worse and Kf1 at least one pawn worse.

items.prompt: White's pawn is on e3 instead of e4. Is castling still the only good move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Castling is among three moves within 0.4 pawns of each other.

hints: Can Black open the centre as quickly now?
Look at how many sensible White moves there are.
Nbd2 and c4 are also fine.
items.explain: With the pawn on e3 the centre is less tense, so castling is one of several good moves rather than the only one. The engine rates O-O, Nbd2 and c4 within 0.4 pawns of each other.

items.prompt: White is a pawn ahead, but his king stands on g1 and Black's queen and rook both aim at g2. Black to move: find the first move of the plan.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is Rxg2+.
Rxg2+ forces mate in six.

hints: List the differences between the two sides. Which one decides the game?
White's king is on the g-file, where two Black pieces aim at g2.
Rxg2+: if the king takes, ...Qg4+ and Black mates.
items.explain: Material says White is better, but the king's position decides. Rxg2+ forces mate in six; White's extra pawn does not matter.

items.prompt: White's king stands on b1 instead of g1. Does the sacrifice Rxg2 still work? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Rxg2 is at least three pawns worse than the best move.

hints: Where is White's king now?
What does the rook on g2 attack when the king is not on the g-file?
Nothing: the rook is simply lost.
items.explain: With the king on b1 there is no mate and Black's queen on h4 is under attack. Rxg2 is at least three pawns worse than the best move. The same attack needs the same target: a plan must fit the position.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is Rxg2+.
Rxg2+ forces mate in seven or fewer.

hints: Compare the two kings. Which one is exposed?
Which squares can Black's queen and rook attack together?
items.explain: White's king on g1 faces the queen and rook on the g-file. Rxg2+ forces mate in at most seven, even though White is a pawn ahead.

items.prompt: White's king stands on b1 instead of g1. Does Rxg2 win for Black? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Rxg2 is at least three pawns worse than the best move.
The engine rates the position at least 1.5 pawns better for White.

hints: Where is White's king?
Does the g-file lead anywhere now?
No: Black's pieces have no target.
items.explain: With the king on b1 the attack has no target, and the engine rates the position at least 1.5 pawns better for White. A plan that worked with the king on g1 does not carry over.

items.prompt: White threatens nothing yet; his pawn cannot advance safely. Black's rook is on the sixth rank. Find a waiting move that keeps the draw. Three moves do.

claims.statement: Exact result from the tablebase: the position is a draw.
The active-looking Rf2 loses.

hints: The rook is well placed on the sixth rank. What should it keep doing?
Move the rook along the sixth rank without leaving it, and do not move the king.
Rb6, Rg6 or Rh6.
items.explain: On the sixth rank the rook keeps White's king from advancing the pawn safely. The tablebase shows exactly three moves keep the draw: Rb6, Rg6 and Rh6. Leaving the rank, for example Rf2, loses.

feedback_by_move.f6f2: Rf2? gives up the sixth rank and White wins (tablebase).
feedback_by_move.e8f7: Kf7? loses (tablebase): the king should stay where it is.

items.prompt: White has pushed the pawn to e6. Black's rook is still on the sixth rank. Does the waiting move Rg6 still keep the draw? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Exact result from the tablebase: Black can still draw.
Rg6 loses.

hints: What has changed since the last position?
The pawn has reached the sixth rank: waiting on that rank is no longer enough.
Rg6 loses. Black must change plan.
items.explain: Waiting was right while the pawn was on e5. With the pawn on e6, Rg6 loses (tablebase), although Black can still draw by another route. Waiting is right only while the opponent has no way forward.

items.prompt: The pawn is on e6 and waiting loses. Find a move that keeps the draw. Three moves do.

claims.statement: Exact result from the tablebase: the position is a draw.

hints: The pawn has advanced, so the old set-up no longer works.
Where can the rook attack the White king and pawn from behind?
Move the rook down the f-file: Rf2, Rf3 or Rf4.
items.explain: Once the pawn has advanced, Black changes plan: the rook leaves the sixth rank for a file where it can check from behind. The tablebase shows exactly Rf2, Rf3 and Rf4 keep the draw.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a move that keeps the draw. Three moves do.

claims.statement: Exact result from the tablebase: the position is a draw.

hints: White cannot make progress yet.
Keep the rook on the sixth rank.
Ra6, Rb6 or Rg6.
items.explain: The pawn is still on the fifth rank, so Black waits: the rook slides along the sixth rank. The tablebase shows three moves keep the draw.

items.prompt: Black to move. Does the waiting move Rb6 keep the draw? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Exact result from the tablebase: Black can still draw.
Rb6 loses.

hints: Where is the pawn now?
Is the opponent still without a way forward?
The pawn is on the sixth rank: Rb6 loses.
items.explain: The pawn has reached the sixth rank, so the waiting move Rb6 loses (tablebase), while Black can still draw by checking from behind. The same move that was right one rank earlier is now wrong.

items.prompt: White's knight on d5 is a strong outpost piece. Black can take it with the knight or with the bishop. Find the better trade.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is Nxd5.
Nxd5 wins a pawn in the engine's best line.
Bxd5 is at least 0.8 pawns worse.

hints: Which Black pieces can capture on d5?
Compare what you give up and what you keep in each case.
Take with the knight and keep the bishop.
items.explain: Both captures remove White's knight, but the engine's first choice is Nxd5, which wins a pawn in its best line, while Bxd5 is at least 0.8 pawns worse. Which piece you give up matters, not only that you trade.

feedback_by_move.e6d5: Bxd5 also removes the knight, but it gives up the wrong piece: it is at least 0.8 pawns worse.

items.prompt: Black could also take the knight with the bishop, 1...Bxd5. Is that as good as 1...Nxd5? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bxd5 is at least 0.8 pawns worse than the best move.

hints: Both moves capture the same knight. What differs?
Which piece is left on the board afterwards?
The engine rates Bxd5 clearly below Nxd5.
items.explain: The same knight is captured, but the engine rates Bxd5 at least 0.8 pawns worse than Nxd5. The trade is only as good as the piece you choose to give up.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is Nxc4.
Nxc4 wins a pawn in the engine's best line.
Nxf3+ is at least one pawn worse.

hints: Black's knight on e5 can capture two different pieces. Which one matters more?
Which White piece is doing more?
Take the bishop on c4.
items.explain: The knight can trade itself for White's bishop on c4 or for the knight on f3. The engine prefers Nxc4, which wins a pawn in its best line, and rates Nxf3+ at least one pawn worse.

items.prompt: Black could instead trade the knight on f3 with 1...Nxf3+. Is that as good as 1...Nxc4? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Nxf3+ is at least one pawn worse than the best move.

hints: Both trades are possible. What does each remove?
Which White piece would be left after Nxf3+ Qxf3?
White keeps the active bishop.
items.explain: Nxf3+ is a trade, but the engine rates it at least one pawn worse than Nxc4. Before you trade, ask which of his pieces you most want gone.
